title: Quiet rollout decision cards — personal index
content:
Purpose: quick-reference index cards for a quiet, low-noise rollout of a model flip + minor runtime change. Keep short, actionable, and easy to copy into alerts or Slack when things get noisy.

Usage: stash this in my personal workspace during the rollout day. Use one card per incident/tie-break decision. Update timestamp and move to the rollout decision log when resolved.

CARD: basic rollout summary
- date: 2025-01-12 (planned)
- cohort: 0.5% warm cohort -> 3% steady -> 10% bulk if green
- model variants: v2-quant (primary), v2-quant-fallback (compat, lower perf)
- runtime change: kernel tweak K-17 tuning enabled (reduced peak mem)
- intent: validate latency tail at 95th and quality on 1k seed prompts
- owner on-call: Liam C (eng-release)

CARD: launch checklist (quick)
- ci green: GH #2893 merged + smoke e2e (deployment-sim) -> ok
- infra: capacity buffer = 20% reserved across west-1 region
- telemetry: delay-free ingestion of traces -> verify pipeline RL-4382
- eval: nightly small eval set run; baseline metrics collected
- comms: one pinned Slack message to #releases + #sre-alerts

CARD: safety watchlist (signals to watch in first 30m)
- latency: p95 > baseline + 40ms OR p99 > baseline + 120ms -> escalate
- errors: 5xx rate > 0.3% sustained > 2m -> rollback trigger (soft)
- correctness: hallucination spike on targeted prompt set (manual check) -> pause and rerun eval set
- cost: token cost per request > 1.5x expected -> investigate batching fallback
- downstream: heavy client backpressure errors or retry storms -> divert traffic

CARD: hard rollback criteria (automated)
- sustained p99 > baseline + 250ms for 5m AND error rate > 1% -> auto pin previous stable (v1)
- application-level SLA breach: any customer SLA violation reported by SRE toolchain -> immediate rollback and incident
- data integrity event (unexpected token leaks or KMS errors) -> immediate full stop, notify security

CARD: soft rollback / mitigation steps
- reduce cohort to previous step (e.g., 3% -> 0.5%) and hold 30m
- enable fallback variant: route new requests to v2-quant-fallback (keeps latency but lowers quality)
- revert kernel tweak: toggle K-17 off on affected nodes (restart pool with drain)
- if front-end retry spikes: add 10s client-side holdoff via edge config and backpressure header

CARD: pinning play (how to pin safely)
- pin command: infra pin-tool set model:v1 --note="auto-pin: rollback after K-17 flip" --owner=Asha
- verify: run smoke generation on pinned release (sanity) -> check tokenization/encoding diffs
- record: create post-pin ticket with short rationale + links to signals that triggered pin

CARD: comms templates (short)
- half-urgent alert to #releases: "Rollout note: observed p95 spike at 12:11 PST, holding at 3% while investigating (Liam). No rollback yet. Logs: <short link>"
- rollback announcement: "Rolling back to v1 across west-1 due to sustained p99 tail. Owner: Asha. Postmortem ticket created: RL-XXXX."

CARD: quick triage matrix (one glance)
- latency-only, p95 spike <60s and no error jump -> mitigation: reduce cohort and monitor (NO PIN)
- error spike > threshold OR client visible failures -> action: soft rollback -> pin if persists
- correctness regressions (manual) -> pause and A/B rerun, hold cohort until quality clears

CARD: telemetry sanity checks to run ASAP
- check APM flame charts for model process CPU stalls across nodes (group by kube node)
- inspect request logs for increased token counts (might indicate prompt truncation changes)
- spot-check servo metrics: cache hit ratio, KV eviction counts
- hit the eval harness with the 1k seed: compare logits/deltas for top-5 tokens

CARD: TODO / followups (after rollout)
- if we rolled back: schedule small canary with no kernel tweak but same model to isolate cause
- add golden prompts to nightly eval that caught the regression; expand seed set by 30%
- write short runbook note for K-17 toggles with exact commands and safety windows
- align with SRE on automated p99 auto-pin thresholds (proposal: >250ms for 5m)

OPEN QUESTIONS (brain-dump)
- should we add an intermediate cohort at 6% between 3% and 10% for better ramping when traffic is bursty? pros/cons?
- do client SDKs need a soft retry header change to avoid amplifying failures? (ask SDK owners Priya)
- are there customers on dedicated that might be affected by kernel K-17 change despite not being in this cohort? check tenancy mapping

NOTES-TO-SELF
- keep this doc tidy; when rollout is complete move the cards into the canonical rollout diary under shared_drives (if it becomes an org-level runbook).
- when in doubt, prefer narrower cohort and manual inspection over aggressive automation for this flip — small perf regressions are survivable, correctness regressions are not.

Last quick snapshot (for checklist copy/paste):
- [ ] Merge GH #2893 -> done? (check)
- [ ] Reserve 20% capacity buffer -> ops ticket created
- [ ] Start 0.5% warm cohort -> note time
- [ ] After 60m, escalate to 3% if signals green -> watch first 30m closely
- [ ] Hold at 3% for minimum 2h before 10% -> run quick eval at +2h

End of index cards. Keep short, keep copyable.
